doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing in Detroit after Snooky Young left
summary: Only Phil Hill's Bluebird quartet was a steady job; he otherwise sat in at jam sessions and played with a short-lived big band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You were describing the musicians. Were there some bands that you typically played in while you were there?

The only band that I spent any length of time with was Philip Hill’s quartet at the Bluebird. There was a big band that was organized by a drummer named Charlie Johnson. They only did two or three engagements. There was another band at the club called the Royal Blue. There were places I’d go sit in. There was a Webster Hall, I think, at Wayne University, where there were regular jam sessions. It was like a student union building. There were regular jam sessions in there. But there was no band that I played with on a regular basis after Snooky Young broke up and they left town, Snooky went back to Ohio, until Philip Hill’s band at the Bluebird.
How would you characterize your period in Detroit in your development? What did that interval of time, how did it serve you?

It served me very well in that that’s where I learned about and how to swing. Before Detroit I was just a good young musician, an accomplished young musician who knew how to read music, who knew how to improvise, and learned how to write, compose and arrange.
